sources.note: Ethnologue: endangered, spoken by the elderly only, no typology field. Wikipedia: ~15 speakers (2000), most Kwerisa have shifted to Kaiy, Kai I village. TransNewGuinea: 37 items all from Voorhoeve 1975. Rosetta list = same Voorhoeve forms. None mention stress or tone.

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane A. 1997. Towards a reconstruction and reclassification of the Lakes Plain languages of Irian Jaya. In Karl Franklin (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics No. 2 (Pacific Linguistics A-85), 133-236. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Kwerisa (56 speakers) is listed p.134 and placed in East Tariku p.155, but p.134 states: 'The languages in the Lakes Plain not included in the study were Kwerisa and Papasena in the Central Lakes Plain Family.. The data available for these languages was considered insufficient for drawing any conclusions'. Family-level only: p.152 sec.11 'Tone is a prominent feature of all Lakes Plain languages.. All the modern languages have at least high and low tone'; p.160 App.3 'stress is not marked because only a few original word lists marked it and it has not been found to be contrastive in any of the…

sources.note: Lexical: Rosetta Swadesh list, Manning 1970 (sil 69139), Briley 1970 (sil 69263), transnewguinea; language descriptions: Glottolog page only. No phonology or grammar exists in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Briley, David. 1970 (14 April). Kwerisa Kai Wordlist. 4 pp., 102 entries, handwritten survey list. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 69263 (draft). Probably the item Glottolog lists as Briley 1978 'Kwerisa' (4 pp.).
sources.note: Independent transcription of the same elicitation (informant Tan, age 13, Kai, 14/4/70, annotated '(Unreliable)'). Stress marks on words (a'bauwe'yaku, 'abi, a'boru, 'tau, 'kwedi, 'su 'wife'), largely agreeing with Manning's; no statement about stress or tone; symbol key blank.

sources.citation: Manning, Margaret. 1970 (14 April). Kwerisa Kaiy Wordlist. 4 pp., 101 entries, handwritten survey list. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 69139 (draft, posted as is).
sources.note: Raw Indonesian-prompt survey wordlist (informant Yan, age 13, Kai village, 14/4/70). Stress is transcribed with IPA ' on many items (a'bau'taru 'shoulder', a'kwau 'lip', 'abi 'tooth', a'boru 'nose', 'tau 'child', 'kwedi 'fire', 'kegi 'one'), but there is no statement about stress; 'Explanation of Symbols:' on p.4 is blank.
